newsitem.title: FRANCE: France seeks French control in Framatome merger.
newsitem.headline: France seeks French control in Framatome merger.

text.p: The French government wants French interests to predominate in the planned merger of nuclear energy group Framatome with Anglo-French joint venture GEC Alsthom, Industry Minister Franck Borotra said on Thursday.

"For the moment negotiations are open. The government has insisted French interests will retain a majority through a core shareholding group after the merger," he said in an interview with financial daily Les Echos.
He reaffirmed that the merger was guided by industrial logic and was one of a series of moves undertaken by the state to take account of globalisation of markets.
Borotra said the state's holding in CEA-Industrie, the main state shareholder in Framatome, was being studied to find the most appropriate way of retaining its stake.
However, one thing was certain, he said. All the activities of Erap, CEA-I and Isis considered non-strategic to the state would be put into the private sector.
Erap is the state's holding company for its equity stake in Elf Aquitaine. Isis is another state holding company.

Asked what the state's plans were for the Cogema nuclear materials group, Borotra said it should not go private but its capital structure should evolve. He was particularly keen its employees should hold shares in the company, the report said.
